definitions.gloss: second person; the grammatical person referring to the listener
definitions.explanation: In grammar, the category of pronouns and verb forms that refer to the person being spoken to — the equivalent of English 'you'. A technical term used in language study, linguistics, and discussions of translation or narrative point of view.

examples.japanese: 「あなた」は{二人称|ににんしょう}{代名詞|だいめいし}です。
この{小説|しょうせつ}は{二人称|ににんしょう}で{書|か}かれている。
examples.english: This novel is written in the second person.

examples.japanese: {日本語|にほんご}では{二人称|ににんしょう}{代名詞|だいめいし}を{省略|しょうりゃく}することが{多|おお}い。
examples.english: In Japanese, second-person pronouns are often omitted.

examples.japanese: {英語|えいご}の you は、{単数|たんすう}でも{複数|ふくすう}でも{同|おな}じ{二人称|ににんしょう}{代名詞|だいめいし}が{使|つか}われる。
examples.english: In English, the same second-person pronoun 'you' is used for both singular and plural.

notes:
Composed of {二|に} (two, second), {人|にん} (person), and {称|しょう} (designation, label). A grammatical term referring to the pronouns and verb forms associated with the addressee.

USAGE:
This is a linguistic or pedagogical term, found mainly in grammar textbooks, language classes, and discussions of writing style. Japanese famously tends to drop pronouns, so the {二人称|ににんしょう} pronouns ({あなた, きみ, おまえ} etc.) appear less often in natural speech than their English counterparts.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {二人称|ににんしょう}{代名詞|だいめいし}: second-person pronoun
- {二人称|ににんしょう}{単数|たんすう}/{複数|ふくすう}: second-person singular / plural
- {二人称|ににんしょう}{視点|してん}: second-person point of view (in writing)
- {二人称|ににんしょう}で{書|か}く: to write in the second person

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {一人称|いちにんしょう}: first person — referring to the speaker (I, we)
- {三人称|さんにんしょう}: third person — referring to someone other than speaker or listener
- {人称|にんしょう}: grammatical person — the general category covering all three
- {代名詞|だいめいし}: pronoun — the broader word class that includes person pronouns
